title: Steering with acceptance criteria
summary: Drake moves the checking to the start: before an agent begins, the task gets a goal, an acceptance check you can observe (an exit code, an output, what it prints), a negative control that proves the check can fail, and what is out of scope. 'It works' is a hope, not acceptance. I can run a checker that holds a task until all four parts are there and the acceptance names something observable.
goal: Hand an agent a task it can finish and you can check.
key_steps: Write the goal in one sentence
Add a negative control that must fail
List what is out of scope
Ask the agent to report against those exact checks

example.code:
note spec: a task is ready for an agent when it has a goal, an observable acceptance check,
note a negative control and what is out of scope
note exit 0 ready, 1 not ready, 2 read error
const NF ulong 4
const KACC ulong 1
const MOK ulong 4
const MMISS ulong 5
const MPASS ulong 6
const MFAIL ulong 7
const MVAGUE ulong 8
const KOBS ulong 9
text KW "Goal:\nAcceptance:\nNegative control:\nOut of scope:\n ok\n MISSING\nREADY: an agent can start, and you can tell when it is done\nNOT READY: tighten the spec before you hand it to an agent\nAcceptance: nothing you could observe (name an exit status, an output, or what it prints)\nexit\noutput\nprints\n"
note helpers: read all of stdin into inb, walk lines, compare a line prefix with the n-th
note entry of the newline separated table KW, and write table entries, input bytes and numbers
global inb uchar 65536
global num uchar 24
fn rdall to long
t = ulong 0
while lt t len inb bound 65536
k = read 0 inb t sub len inb t
if lt k 0
ret k
end
if eq k 0
ret long t
end
t = add t ulong k
end
ret neg long 27
end
fn eol s ulong n ulong to ulong
i = s
while lt i n bound 65536
if eq get inb i 10
ret i
end
i = add i 1
end
ret n
end
fn kstart k ulong to ulong
p = ulong 0
c = ulong 0
while lt c k bound 4096
if eq get KW p 10
c = add c 1
end
p = add p 1
end
ret p
end
fn klen k ulong to ulong
s = kstart k
i = s
while ne get KW i 10 bound 4096
i = add i 1
end
ret sub i s
end
fn pmat at ulong e ulong k ulong to bool
o = kstart k
m = klen k
if gt m sub e at
ret false
end
for j ulong m
if ne get inb add at j get KW add o j
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
fn emitk o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 4096
w = write 1 KW add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emiti o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 65536
w = write 1 inb add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emitn o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 24
w = write 1 num add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn say k ulong to void
emitk kstart k add klen k 1
end
fn word k ulong to void
emitk kstart k klen k
end
fn emitu v ulong to void
p = ulong 24
x = v
while true bound 21
p = sub p 1
put num p uchar add rem x 10 48
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
emitn p sub 24 p
end
fn filled at ulong e ulong to bool
i = at
while lt i e bound 65536
if ne get inb i 32
ret true
end
i = add i 1
end
ret false
end
fn has k ulong n ulong to bool
s = ulong 0
while lt s n bound 65536
e = eol s n
if pmat s e k
if filled add s klen k e
ret true
end
end
s = add e 1
end
ret false
end
fn within s ulong e ulong k ulong to bool
i = s
while lt i e bound 65536
if pmat i e k
ret true
end
i = add i 1
end
ret false
end
fn observ n ulong to bool
s = ulong 0
while lt s n bound 65536
e = eol s n
if pmat s e KACC
for k ulong 3
if within s e add KOBS k
ret true
end
end
end
s = add e 1
end
ret false
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 2
end
n = ulong r
miss = ulong 0
for k ulong NF
word k
if has k n
say MOK
else
say MMISS
miss = add miss 1
end
end
if has KACC n
if not observ n
say MVAGUE
miss = add miss 1
end
end
if eq miss 0
say MPASS
ret 0
end
say MFAIL
ret 1
end

common_mistake: Giving a vague task and steering afterwards, round after round. Each correction is acceptance criteria you could have written up front. Fix: two minutes on goal, observable acceptance, negative control and scope before the agent starts.
evidence_note: The example compiled and ran on a Linux ARM64 computer (no GPU) and its output is recorded byte for byte, including a negative control. Rests on the recorded run: a complete spec was READY (exit 0); a spec whose acceptance was 'it works' and one missing control and scope were held (exit 1). NOT done: the checker checks the shape of a task; it accepted 'none needed' as a negative control, and judging content stays with you.
